Use this tool after deciding how the holder should stand. It generates **support parts**, matching slot geometry and a fit coupon. It does not prove that a stand is stable or strong enough. Measure the real material, test the joint, and load-test the assembled prototype.

## Choose the support by the force path

- **Straight tabbed leg:** compact and easy to place, but it can act like a cantilever when the load is offset.
- **Angled tabbed leg:** moves the contact point outward and increases the footprint. Use a pair so the holder does not twist.
- **Triangular support:** turns bending into a shorter compression path and is usually the stiffest simple side profile.
- **Rear easel leg:** works with a front frame and pivot to make a three-point footprint. Keep useful material around the pivot hole.
- **Cross-foot pair:** two half-slotted strips make a wide, removable base. Test the slot because both parts depend on the same fit.

The purple coupon tests the chosen tab length and calculated slot width. Blue slot rectangles are **mating geometry to position in the holder plate**, not separate finished parts.

## Before cutting

1. Measure the actual sheet thickness in several places.
2. Cut the fit coupon before the complete legs.
3. Open the SVG in Inkscape and confirm its millimetre dimensions at 100% scale.
4. Place matching slots in the holder plate and check that each slot has enough material around it.
5. Prototype in cardboard or scrap stock.
6. Assemble the real holder and test front-to-back and side-to-side tipping.

Read [Make It Stand](../../03-laser-cutting/02-make-it-stand.qmd) for the easel force diagrams, bending explanation, starting proportions and external reference templates. Use the [Fabrication Plate Builder](../plate-builder/index.qmd) for the holder plate and repeated holes.
